content.value_statement: API integrations often fail because authentication, retries, and rate limits are incomplete. This skill guides robust clients, OAuth flows, webhook verification, and operational checks.
actual_capabilities: Explains API key, OAuth 2.0, JWT, and webhook authentication patterns.
Provides JavaScript examples for request wrappers, retries, rate limiting, pagination, and response mapping.
Shows Stripe, SendGrid, and Twilio integration examples using environment variables.
Lists troubleshooting checks for authentication, rate limits, timeouts, and scopes.
Recommends monitoring practices for response times, errors, usage, and health checks.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not provide executable tools or tests.
Examples are JavaScript focused and may need adaptation for other languages.
It does not cover every provider-specific SDK or security requirement.
Webhook examples should be hardened with provider-specific verification rules.

use_cases.title: Plan a New API Client
use_cases.description: Design authentication, request structure, error handling, retries, and rate limiting before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Harden Webhook Processing
use_cases.description: Review signature verification, payload parsing, event handling, and response behavior for third-party webhooks.

use_cases.title: Debug Integration Failures
use_cases.description: Use structured checks for authentication errors, rate limits, timeout failures, and missing provider scopes.

prompt_templates.title: Start an API Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a REST API integration for my application. Cover authentication, request structure, error handling, rate limits, and testing needs.

prompt_templates.title: Review Client Reliability
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my API client design for retries, timeouts, pagination, response mapping, and rate limit handling. Point out missing reliability safeguards.

prompt_templates.title: Design Webhook Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design webhook handling for a third-party provider. Include signature verification, duplicate event handling, logging, and failure responses.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this production API integration plan for security, observability, cost controls, provider limits, incident response, and credential rotation.

output_examples.input: Review my planned payment API client for production readiness.
output: Validate that credentials come from managed secrets and are never logged.
Add request timeouts, exponential backoff, and clear retry limits for server errors.
Track response time, failure rate, rate limit usage, and payment outcome events.

output_examples.input: Help troubleshoot failed webhook deliveries from a provider.
output: Confirm the endpoint accepts the provider content type and returns success quickly.
Verify signature calculation with the raw request body and current secret.
Check replay protection, duplicate event handling, and retry logs.

output_examples.output: Use cursor or next-page metadata from the provider, process pages incrementally, and stop only when the provider indicates completion.

best_practices: Keep credentials in environment variables or a managed secret store.
Set timeouts, retry limits, and rate limit handling before production release.
Log enough request context to debug failures without recording secrets.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding API keys, tokens, webhook secrets, or account identifiers in source files.
Retrying every failed request without checking status codes or idempotency.
Accepting webhook payloads before validating signatures and duplicate delivery behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill execute API calls for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for building API integrations in your own codebase.

faq.question: Which API styles does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers REST clients, OAuth flows, API keys, webhooks, pagination, and common provider SDK examples.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It discusses secret storage, HTTPS, webhook signatures, request signing, and key rotation.

faq.question: Are the examples production ready as written?
faq.answer: No. Treat them as patterns and adapt them to provider documentation, tests, and your runtime.

faq.question: What should I prepare before using it?
faq.answer: Collect provider documentation, authentication details, rate limits, webhook requirements, and current failure logs.
